title: MINOS: Distributed Consistency and Persistency Protocol Implementation & Offloading to SmartNICs
problem: Implementing Distributed Data Persistency (DDP) models for leaderless systems is complex, requiring support for linearizable consistency with multiple persistency guarantee types. Current implementations face performance limitations due to high request latency and throughput constraints.
motivation: Distributed systems require high-performance, programmable, and resilient architectures to ensure data consistency and persistency guarantees in leaderless systems.
method: The paper develops algorithms (MINOS-B) supporting linearizable consistency—where all participants see identical data—with five different persistence guarantee types, tested on 5-node clusters. To improve performance, they move these algorithms to a SmartNIC (a specialized network card with computing power, version MINOS-O), which uses selective coherence hardware (maintaining data consistency only where needed), message batching (combining multiple messages before sending), and broadcast optimizations (speeding up messages sent to multiple recipients).
key_novelty: The key idea is offloading consistency and persistency protocols to a SmartNIC (a specialized network card) with selective coherence hardware to improve performance.
contributions: Detailed distributed algorithms for DDP models supporting linearizable consistency with five persistency types
MINOS-Baseline implementation and evaluation on 5-node distributed systems
SmartNIC-based offloading architecture with selective coherence, message batching, and broadcasting optimizations
Demonstration of 35% latency reduction and throughput improvements through hardware offloading

metrics.speedup: 35% end-to-end latency reduction, increased request throughput
